title: UNESCO / ITU Global ICT Skills: Youth Programming Proficiency, Tertiary STEM Pipeline, and High-Skill Employment
source_name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) & International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
description: Cross-national empirical indicators tracking SDG 4.4.1 youth programming skills, complex data analysis competencies, tertiary STEM graduation pipelines, and high-skill technology employment rates across advanced economies.
observation_unit: Cross-national panel across ITU/UNESCO reporting jurisdictions
sample_population_note: National representative household surveys of individuals aged 15-24
sample_population_size: Standardized ITU national household sample frames
title_ja: 【UNESCO/ITU】若年層プログラミング技能・高度データ活用とハイテク雇用の多変量分析

research_angles.title: The Digital Native Operational Illusion: Why High Device Saturation Fails to Guarantee Production-Level Computing Competencies
research_questions: Does ubiquitous consumer digital device adoption automatically foster programming and data analysis proficiency?
How strongly does the secondary programming skill rate predict subsequent tertiary STEM graduation and tech employment?
hypotheses: Youth programming skill rate exhibits a strong positive relationship with high-skill tech employment (VIF < 2.0).
Passive smartphone usage does not organically translate into algorithmic programming without formal curriculum integration.
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Human Capital Theory (Becker) and Computational Thinking Framework (Wing)
